To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bcl- 2 mRNA encodes a protein that is homolgous to a predicted EBV protein, that most t(14; 18) breakpoints cluster within a long exon, and that the t(14:18) translocation produces a hybrid bcl2/ Ig mRNA.

1) the Bcl-2 protein has an amino acid sequence homologous to that of the predicted Epstein-Barr Virus protein BHRF1, 2) t(14; 18) translocations cluster within a 5. 4 kb region that contains the 3' end of the Bcl- 2 gene, 3) t(14,18) translocations produce hybrid Bcl- 1/immunoglobuin heavy chain mRNA's,
the BCL-2 gene, located on chromosome 18, is rearranged in follicular lymphoma and that BCL-2 is a novel gene product that is homologus to a protein encoded by an EBV gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, cloning and characterization of the human BCL-2 oncogene.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of B cell lymphomas.
the molecular mechanisms of the t(14:18) translocation in B-cell neoplasia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
t(14,18) translocation is the most common chromosomal translocation in B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
bcl-2 is a proto-oncogene and that its deregulation is involved in lymphomagenesis.
the BCL2 oncogene is a proto-oncogene, and that its activation by chromosomal translocation in human follicular lymphoma is the result of an aberrant transcription of the gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
t(14:18) translocations result in abnormal expression of a gene, bcl-2, whose product has a homology with a viral protein and that is involved in the control of cell proliferation.
the BCL2 protooncogene is a candidate for the role of a growth factor receptor, or an oncogene that is activated by chromosomal translocations.
the bcl-1 gene is located on chromosome 14, and the bcl-3 gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 18.
The main takeaway from our work is that
t(14:18) translocations in follicular lymphoma lead to the production of a hybrid bcl2/Ig heavy chain mRNA.
t(14,18) translocations result in the production of bcl-1/immunoglobulins heavy chain hybrid mRNAs that continue to encode the bcl-1 gene product.
t(14:18) translocations in follicular lymphomas result in the formation of a hybrid mRNA that is translated into a normal bcl2 protein.
